cultural_tradition: Video game RPG (Mass Effect series; BioWare)
source_citation: Mass Effect (BioWare, 2007): biotic amps are cranial implants that amplify biotic abilities (gravity manipulation, warp fields, singularity); Mass Effect 2 / 3 refine the amp taxonomy; canonically gravity/mass-coded = earth-primary per physical-force analogy; Codex entry: 'biotic amps boost the electrical signal from the brain to the biotic implant'

cultural_tradition: Urban fantasy fiction (The Dresden Files; Jim Butcher)
form: rod (carved-wood blasting-focus; caster-implement for fire-spell channeling)
source_citation: Storm Front (Jim Butcher, 2000) ch. 2: Harry Dresden uses a blasting rod carved from a carved wooden rod to channel fire-magic; Through the entire Dresden Files series the blasting rod is his canonical fire-focus (distinct from his staff which is general-purpose); Dead Beat (2005) and Changes (2010) feature the rod prominently as fire-primary implement

cultural_tradition: Tabletop sci-fi RPG (Eclipse Phase; Posthuman Studios)
source_citation: Eclipse Phase 1st Edition (Posthuman Studios, 2009) ch. 7: Async rules — psi-chi sleights are subconscious passive abilities including enhanced cognition and sense manipulation; asynch characters are 'infected' by the Watts-MacLeod strain of the Exsurgent virus, which is canonically shadow/void-register; Eclipse Phase is explicitly cited in the dispatch as a canonical modern-caster tabletop sci-fi source
